subtopic: ONNX / Versioning, IR version vs Opset version
learningObjective: Distinguish ONNX's IR version (model format) from opset version (operator semantics).
stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes ONNX's IR version from its opset version?

options.text: IR version and opset version are two names for the same field; both refer to the operator set used by the model.

IR version defines the on-disk protobuf schema/structural features of ModelProto (e.g., which optional fields exist); opset version defines the semantics of individual operators (e.g., what attributes Conv accepts). The two evolve independently, and a model must declare both.
IR version is used only during export; runtimes ignore it and only look at the opset when executing.
Opset version is a subset of IR version: opset N is always the operator content of IR version N; both must be equal in every valid ONNX model.

explanation: ONNX has two distinct versioning axes: (1) IR version — the ModelProto schema version, defining structural/format features (e.g., what fields exist, how initializers are stored); (2) Opset version(s) — the semantic version of each operator domain. A model declares its `ir_version` and one or more `opset_import` entries. These evolve independently: adding a new opset does not typically require a new IR version, and vice versa.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: IR version = format schema; opset version = operator semantics.
optionExplanations.A: Wrong: they are different fields with different roles.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: IR version affects how the runtime parses the file.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: they are not tied numerically.

assumptions: ONNX specification distinction between IR version and opset version.
nonImplications: Does not imply a runtime supporting one high IR version supports all opsets.
Does not imply IR versions are backward-compatible without effort.

distractorRationales.C: Ignores IR version's role in parsing.
